mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi engine typically costs £1,900-£3,500 supply-only, depending on power output and supplier. DW10FC 150hp units start around £1,900, while 180hp units range £2,000-£3,500. The older DW10BTED4 (RHR) units range £1,800-£3,200. Used engines start from £1,200. Supply & fit adds £400-£900 labour. Main dealer replacement can exceed £6,500.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi (DW10FC) engine problems are DPF regeneration failure causing loss of power and limp mode, EGR cooler failure causing coolant loss and white smoke, injector seal wear causing oil dilution, and AdBlue system faults triggering countdowns. The 2.0 BlueHDi is generally more robust than the 1.6L unit but shares emissions system vulnerabilities.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound. A rebuilt unit costs £1,900-£3,500 versus £6,000-£18,000 for a comparable used 3008. With dealer replacement potentially exceeding £6,500, specialist rebuilt units offer significant savings. The 2.0 BlueHDi's strong torque and towing capability make it a desirable engine - replacement often makes sense for well-maintained GT and Allure trims.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi (DW10FC) engine typically reaches 150,000-200,000 miles. Regular oil changes, DPF-friendly driving (regular motorway runs) and AdBlue system maintenance are essential for longevity. The DW10 family is generally considered one of the most reliable diesel engines in the Peugeot range, with many examples exceeding 200,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi and 2.0 HDi engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.0 BlueHDi (DW10FC) is a Euro 6 diesel introduced in 2016, featuring AdBlue (SCR) for lower NOx emissions. The 2.0 HDi (DW10BTED4/RHR) is a Euro 5 diesel from 2009-2016 without AdBlue. Both use the same 2.0L (1,997cc) DW10 architecture, but the BlueHDi has more complex emissions hardware and is generally more fuel-efficient. The BlueHDi is also more sensitive to short-journey driving patterns due to its DPF and AdBlue systems.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi engine code is DW10FC (RHE) for second-generation models (2016-2024) or DW10BTED4 (RHR) for first-generation models (2009-2016). It appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi (DW10FC) is the performance diesel option for the second-generation (2016-present) 3008, delivering strong torque, excellent towing capability and refined motorway cruising. Part of Stellantis's DW10 engine family, the 2.0 BlueHDi produces up to 180hp and offers the best balance of power and economy for GT and high-spec trims. Available in 150hp and 180hp outputs, it powers Allure, GT Line and GT variants - but its complex AdBlue system and DPF maintenance requirements have made it a source of replacement enquiries for high-mileage examples. A limited number of first-generation facelift models (2013-2016) also used the DW10BTED4 (RHR) 2.0 HDi engine, which shares similar architecture but lacks the AdBlue system of the BlueHDi.

milestones.description: **2013** - Facelift models carry forward DW10BTED4 with minor emissions updates
**2016** - Second-generation 3008 launched with DW10FC (RHE) 2.0 BlueHDi 150hp and 180hp
**2017** - DW10FC becomes the performance diesel option for GT and GT Line trims
**2019** - Minor ECU refinements to improve DPF regeneration and AdBlue calibration
**2021** - 2.0 BlueHDi continues as the flagship diesel for GT models
**2024** - Final production of 2.0 BlueHDi as Peugeot transitions to electrified powertrains

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every DW10FC and DW10BTED4 engine fitted to the Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi (DW10FC) is a robust, high-torque diesel - but its complex emissions hardware and high-mileage wear patterns create distinct failure points. DPF regeneration failure, EGR cooler leaks and injector seal wear are the primary drivers of replacement enquiries. The DW10 family is generally considered one of the most reliable diesel engines in the Peugeot range when properly maintained, but the AdBlue system adds complexity to the BlueHDi variants. Every rebuilt Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF Regeneration Failure - Why Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi Engines Lose Power
problems.rootCause: Short-journey driving prevents the DPF from reaching regeneration temperature, causing soot buildup that blocks exhaust flow. The 2.0 BlueHDi's DPF is sensitive to urban driving patterns, and regeneration requires sustained motorway speeds to complete effectively. The DW10FC is particularly susceptible to DPF-related faults if used predominantly for city driving.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic reset, extended high-speed drive or forced regen cycle
repairOptions.longevity: Works if blockage is early-stage and sensors are functional

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove DPF for off-car cleaning or supply fitted replacement unit
repairOptions.longevity: Restores function if substrate isn't melted or cracked

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with new DPF, EGR and AdBlue components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Needed if blockage caused turbo or piston damage

problems.recommendation: For a Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi used mainly for short trips, invest in regular motorway runs to allow DPF regeneration. The 2.0 BlueHDi's DPF is larger and more robust than the 1.6L unit, but still requires attention. If the anti-pollution warning appears, address it promptly. A rebuilt engine is only necessary if the DPF has caused turbo or internal damage - the DW10FC block is generally robust and can be saved if caught early.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DW10FC Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi engine prices

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Failure - Why Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi Engines Lose Coolant
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler can develop micro-fractures in its weld seams, allowing coolant to leak into the exhaust manifold or combustion chambers. This leads to coolant loss, white smoke from the exhaust and, in severe cases, hydrolock. The DW10BTED4 (pre-BlueHDi) is particularly prone to this issue due to its earlier cooler design, but the DW10FC can also suffer from cooler failure at higher mileages.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of EGR cooler, coolant flush, system pressure test
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before engine damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with new EGR cooler, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if cooler failure has caused cylinder head or piston damage

problems.recommendation: EGR cooler failure on the Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi should be addressed immediately. If you notice unexplained coolant loss or sweet exhaust smell, have the EGR cooler inspected. Replacing the cooler is a straightforward specialist job. A rebuilt engine is only necessary if coolant has entered the combustion chambers causing hydrolock or piston damage.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DW10FC Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi engine prices

problems.h4: Injector Seal Wear - Why Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi Engines Suffer Oil Dilution
problems.rootCause: Injector seals degrade over time, allowing combustion gases to leak past the injector and causing oil dilution. The DW10FC's injector design is generally robust, but high-mileage examples can develop seal wear, leading to increased oil levels, reduced lubrication and potential engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removal of injectors, replacement of seals, recutting of injector seats
Supply & fit rebuilt unit with new injectors and seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if injector failure has caused cylinder head damage

problems.recommendation: Injector seal wear on the Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi is less common than on the 1.6L units but should still be addressed promptly. If you notice rising oil levels or a diesel smell in the oil, have the injector seals inspected. A specialist can replace seals and recut seats in around four hours. If the vehicle has a history of multiple injector failures or the head is damaged, a rebuilt engine may be more cost-effective.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DW10FC Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi engine prices

problems.h4: AdBlue System Faults - Why Peugeot 3008 2.0 BlueHDi Engines Trigger Countdowns
problems.rootCause: Crystallised urea deposits clog the AdBlue injector nozzle, triggering fault codes and eventually a countdown to engine immobilisation. The 2.0 BlueHDi's AdBlue system is similar to the 1.6L but may have different sensor calibration. Sensor faults are also common, triggering "AdBlue system fault" warnings.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injector, ultrasonic clean, system reset, test drive
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before countdown reaches zero

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply and fit new AdBlue injector, recalibrate system
repairOptions.longevity: Restores function; may need tank flush if contamination severe

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with new emissions hardware, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if injector failure led to NOx damage or engine derate

problems.recommendation: Address AdBlue warnings immediately - a £120-£300 specialist clean can prevent a £700 injector replacement. If the countdown has started, act fast to avoid immobilisation. Replacement engines are only needed if the fault caused secondary damage. The 2.0 BlueHDi's AdBlue system is generally reliable when maintained with genuine AdBlue fluid.
